title_en: Spending in the Path of God
body_ar: استخلفنا الله عز وجل على الأموال التي بين أيدينا، وحثنا سبحانه على الإنفاق في سبيله، وبين لنا حقارة هذه الحياة الدنيا، حتى لا نغتر بزينتها، فمن يوق شح نفسه، وينفق مما آتاه الله؛ فهو من المفلحين. مسائل في الإنفاق في سبيل الله : الحكمة من الأمر بالإنفاق في سبيل الله: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه، واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى جعل التكليف امتحاناً لبني آدم، وجعل رضاه فيما كان مخالفاً للهوى، فللإنسان هوىً يدعوه إلى الانسياق وراءه، فمن انساق وراءه لم ينجح في أي امتحان، ومن خالف هواه فإن الله وعده على ذلك بالجنة...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God, mighty and majestic, has made us stewards over the wealth that is in our hands; He has urged us, glorified is He, to spend in His path; and He has made plain to us the paltriness of this worldly life, so that we should not be deceived by its adornment. Whoever is guarded against the avarice of his own soul, and spends of what God has given him, is among the successful.

## Questions on spending in the path of God: the wisdom behind the command to spend in the path of God

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted is He, has made legal obligation a test for the children of Adam, and has placed His good pleasure in what runs counter to caprice. A person has a caprice calling him to be drawn along after it; whoever is drawn along after it succeeds in no test, and whoever goes against his caprice — God has promised him Paradise for that...

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
The CMS timestamp, 5 May 2011, is an upload date and must not be presented as the date the lesson was given.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the transcribed portion; 'التكليف' is rendered 'legal obligation' in its general sense of being placed under the law, not as any one of the five rulings.
